clue.text: Old Bob experiencing heavy going in Dreamland

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling, the old pre-decimal coin abbreviated S
moving heavily and clumsily is lumbering

explanation.surface: An elderly man called Bob is plodding wearily through a dream world.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the old British shilling, written S; 'experiencing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asleep and dreaming is in the land of nod, i.e. sleeping soundly.

clue.text: Made out one, hastened to grasp it

indicators.note: to grasp means the hastened word holds the one piece inside it

parts.note: sped means hastened
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a thing and rushed to grab it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the one; a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out something in the distance is to discern or catch sight of it.

clue.text: Stress the position of the sleeper

explanation.surface: Emphasis is given to where someone lies asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: A railway sleeper is the beam laid beneath the rails, so its position is under the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it; a railway sleeper lies beneath the track.

clue.text: Main entrance for a Victorian beauty

definitions.text: Main entrance for a Victorian beauty

parts.words: Main entrance for a Victorian beauty
parts.note: the main is the sea, and this was the wheeled cabin through which a Victorian lady entered the water

explanation.surface: The front door used by a lovely nineteenth-century woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like the principal door; it is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathing machine was a hut on wheels rolled into the sea so bathers could change and enter unseen.

clue.text: Relinquishes rules about head of State

indicators.note: about says the rules word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a monarch who rules reigns

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word State

explanation.surface: A ruler gives up control because of the head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up or surrender an office.

clue.text: Yorkshire river spirit turns ' up in Africa

indicators.note: turns says the spirit word next to it is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: gin is a spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the river name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A drink by a northern English river surfaces in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes NIG of GIN and 'up' makes ERIA of AIRE; read together they also reverse AIRE + GIN as one run. Yorkshire is a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a West African country, so it lies on that continent.

clue.text: Fuel oil prepared against red revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word red is read backwards

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Fuel is being made ready for a socialist uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' turns RED into DER; 'prepared' is a link. DERV is the British name for diesel road fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: DERV (diesel-engined road vehicle) is the British term for diesel, an oil used as fuel.

clue.text: Postwoman in USA ?

parts.note: not a mail carrier but a woman surnamed Post, the famous American etiquette writer

explanation.surface: A female mail carrier in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Emily Post was an American writer on etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Post is the given name of the American author of Etiquette.

clue.text: Watchword of a Church of England living perhaps

definitions.text: Watchword of a Church of England living perhaps

parts.words: Watchword of a Church of England living perhaps
parts.note: a word meaning watchfulness, made of vigil, a church service held through the night, as if it were a motto for a parish

explanation.surface: The motto of an Anglican parish.
explanation.walkthrough: A vigil is both a night watch and a church service on the eve of a feast, so the word suits a church living as a motto.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilance is watchfulness, keeping awake and alert to danger.

clue.text: Words on the wall in worse shape for one with a sharp appetite

indicators.note: in worse shape suggests the words are in a poor state, rearranged

explanation.surface: Graffiti on a wall has deteriorated, written by someone hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in worse shape' signals the anagram of WORDS, WALL and WORSE; 'on the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword-swallower is a performer who swallows blades, so has a taste for sharp things.

clue.text: Writes for charges, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to charge formally with a crime is to indict; indicts is said with a silent c

explanation.surface: Someone composes letters in return for a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: INDICTS is pronounced 'in-dites', so it gives the homophone INDITES.
explanation.definitionFit: To indite is an old word for composing or putting into writing.

clue.text: Jester returns to monarch looking like a fool

indicators.note: returns means the jester word comes back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: a wag is a joker or jester
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A court jester goes back to his king, who looks foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns WAG into GAW; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Staring stupidly is gawking, the behaviour of a gawk or simpleton.

clue.text: Firearm for, the German campanologist

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a campanologist is a bell ringer

explanation.surface: A German bell-ringer is being offered a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for,' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket pistol, named after its American maker.

clue.text: Can a lory be a sort of sail?

indicators.note: Can ... be asks whether the letters of a lory could become something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a parrot could serve as a sail.
explanation.walkthrough: A lory is a kind of parrot; 'Can ... be' asks whether its letters can be rearranged, and they give ROYAL.
explanation.definitionFit: On a square-rigged ship the royal is the small sail set above the topgallant.

clue.text: Hang jazz !

explanation.surface: An order to execute jazz musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang is to sway or swing from a rope, and swing is a style of big-band jazz.

clue.text: Adherent has extra wine inside

indicators.note: has ... inside means the extra word holds the wine word within it

parts.note: super means extra, as in super-fine
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A follower is carrying an additional bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter is a follower or partisan of a cause.

clue.text: Arrival of Leda's lover reported by powder-puff maker

explanation.surface: News of a swan landing comes from a cosmetics manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Zeus came to Leda as a swan, so news that he has landed reads 'swan's down'; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a report that the bird has landed; the second is the soft swan feathers once used to make powder puffs.

clue.text: Tail-less gibbon a lot of trouble — bars essential

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
tail-less means the gibbon loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An ape without a tail causes great nuisance behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail-less' cuts GIBBON to GIBBO, and 'trouble' rearranges GIBBO plus A LOT; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an obbligato is an accompanying part that must not be left out of the score.

clue.text: Revolution in state advanced, becoming widespread

indicators.note: in means the revolution piece sits inside the state piece

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania
rev is a common short form of revolution, as in revs per minute
money advanced as a loan has been lent

explanation.surface: An uprising in a country advanced until it was felt everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is common and found everywhere, just as widespread things are.

clue.text: Being an old Jewish ascetic about 100

indicators.note: about says the ascetic word wraps round the number

parts.note: the Essenes were an ancient Jewish ascetic sect
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A Jewish hermit of ancient times is around a hundred years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence means a thing's fundamental nature, its very existence.

clue.text: With canned hog's bead Edward lost weight

annotationWithheld.why: With canned hog's-head Edward lost weight (7): TINNED (canned) plus H (hog's head) gives the answer, leaving Edward unused; TIN+H+NED needs canned as both TIN and the container
annotationWithheld.clue: With canned hog's bead Edward lost weight

clue.text: Go easy with early cereal in France

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is the early part of the day
ble is French for wheat

explanation.surface: Advice to take it slowly when eating breakfast cereal in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk at a leisurely pace is to stroll or saunter without hurry.

clue.text: This sex-appeal disturbed Homo Sap

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters of this word plus the sex-appeal piece are jumbled to form homo sap

parts.note: SA is the standard abbreviation for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Sexual attraction has upset the human race.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus SA, jumbled ('disturbed'), make HOMO SAP; take SA out of those letters and what is left rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is slang for sexual allure, sheer physical attractiveness.

clue.text: State the most important point

parts.note: main means chief or most important
E for east is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone declares the central issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb; it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost state of the USA.

clue.text: Picture that has yet to go west?

definitions.text: Picture that has yet to go west?

parts.words: Picture that has yet to go west?
parts.note: a painting of objects; read literally, something that still has life, not yet having gone west, i.e. died

explanation.surface: A painting that has not yet been taken to America.
explanation.walkthrough: To go west is slang for to die, so something that has not yet gone west still has life.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a painting of inanimate objects such as fruit or flowers.

clue.text: Donne — new edition in current series

indicators.note: a new edition reworks the text, so the poet's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh printing of the poet John Donne joins the latest series of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Things placed end-on meet tip to tip in a continuous line, like components in a series.

clue.text: Grand palace in Austria ? Nonsense

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the idea that the great palace is in Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand Trianon is a palace in the grounds of Versailles, in France, not Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Trianon is a small royal residence built for Louis XIV near Versailles.

clue.text: Fresh face — coming back fresher than fresh

parts.note: new means fresh

indicators.note: coming back means the face word returns, read the other way

parts.note: dial is slang for a face

explanation.surface: A youthful face returns, looking even more youthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns DIAL into LAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs just produced by the hen are as fresh as eggs can be.

clue.text: Part of a film dance

explanation.surface: A sequence of a movie shows people dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool of cinema film, and also a lively Scottish country dance.

clue.text: S Meat gives gentle lion tummy trouble

parts.note: tender means gentle

indicators.note: tummy trouble suggests the word lion is churned up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating meat upsets the stomach of a mild-mannered lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tummy trouble' rearranges LION into LOIN; 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is the most tender cut of beef or pork, from the loin.
